title: Try Cargo Without an Account: Browse Go-to-Market Actions, Dry Run One, Plan a Project
summary: What works in Cargo before you sign up: list every connector and native action with its credit price, dry run one for free, and plan a project offline with the cargo-ai CLI, or browse the catalog from any agent through the public MCP server at mcp.getcargo.io/public. Every command, what it returns, and what still needs an account.
body_markdown:
**Yes, you can try Cargo without an account. With no sign-in and no API key, the` cargo-ai` CLI lists every connector and native action with its credit price, dry runs a connector or native action for free, and plans a project offline; the public MCP server at` https://mcp.getcargo.io/public` serves the same catalog to any agent.** Running an action and deploying a project are what need an account.


Without an account Needs an account


` cargo-ai orchestration action list` : actions and their credit prices` action execute` and` execute-batch` without` --dry-run`


` cargo-ai connection integration list` ,` get` ,` get-documentation` Your workspace’s own tools, agents and models


` cargo-ai orchestration action execute --dry-run` : sample result and price` get-output-schema` for an action whose output depends on its configuration


` cargo-ai project init` ,` types` ,` check` ,` info` ,` plan`` cargo-ai project deploy` , and a live diff against what is deployed


` search_actions` and` get_action_schema` on` mcp.getcargo.io/public`` execute_action` and the rest of` mcp.getcargo.io/mcp`


## 1. Install the CLI#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   --version     # 1.0.122 or later


```


This is Cargo the go-to-market platform, not Rust’s` cargo` . Signed-out commands arrived in version 1.0.122; an older install answers every command with “Not authenticated”. If the global install is not on your` PATH` ,` npx @cargo-ai/cli` works in place of` cargo-ai` .


Every command below prints its JSON on stdout. Signed out, it also prints one line on stderr, so an agent parsing stdout is not affected:


text


```text
Not signed in: reading the official integrations and their actions only. Sign up with `cargo-ai login --email you@company.com` (100 free credits, no card) to run one.


```


## 2. Browse every action and its price#


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   list   find   work   email


```


All query terms must match. Each result names the action, the integration, and the exact` action` object the other commands take:


json


```text
{
"query"  :   "find work email"  ,
"totalMatches"  :   1  ,
"results"  : [
{
"name"  :   "Find work email"  ,
"description"  :   "Find a person's work email"  ,
"integrationName"  :   "Forager"  ,
"category"  :   "enrichment"  ,
"credits"  : [
{
"config"  : {   "jsonSchema"  : {   "type"  :   "object"   } },
"cost"  :   2  ,
"type"  :   "fixed"
}
],
"action"  : {
"kind"  :   "connector"  ,
"integrationSlug"  :   "forager"  ,
"actionSlug"  :   "findWorkEmail"
}
}
]
}


```


The` credits` array is the price, read from the catalog at the moment you run the command. It takes one of three shapes:` fixed` is` cost` credits per call,` unit` is` cost` per unit returned plus` fixedCost` per call, and` package` is` cost` per block of` unitsCount` units plus` fixedCost` . An action with no` credits` array costs no credits.


Narrow the list with` --kind connector` or` --kind native` ,` --integration-slug <slug>` ,` --category enrichment` (or sales, marketing, engagement and the rest), and` --limit <n>` . To read a whole integration instead:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   connection   integration   list   --summary             # slug, name and category of each
cargo-ai   connection   integration   get   hubspot                # its actions, schemas and prices
cargo-ai   connection   integration   get-documentation   hubspot


```


Signed out, these return the official integrations and Cargo’s native actions.` --kind tool` and` --kind agent` return nothing, because tools and agents belong to a workspace.


## 3. Dry run one action, for free#


Add` --dry-run` to` action execute` and nothing runs. The CLI reads the action’s definition, checks your` --data` against its input schema, prices the call, and prints a sample result in the shape of a finished run:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"aiArk","actionSlug":"enrichCompany"}'   \
--data   '{"domain":"example.com"}'   \
--dry-run


```


json


```text
{
"run"  : {
"status"  :   "success"  ,
"executions"  : [
{
"nodeSlug"  :   "action"  ,
"title"  :   "Enrich company"  ,
"status"  :   "success"  ,
"creditsUsedCount"  :   0
}
]
},
"runContext"  : {
"action"  : {
"name"  :   "Example Inc"  ,
"domain"  :   "example.com"  ,
"industry"  :   "Software"  ,
"employee_count"  :   120  ,
"country"  :   "United States"  ,
"technologies"  : [  "sample"  ]
}
},
"runComputedConfigs"  : {   "action"  : {   "domain"  :   "example.com"   } },
"dryRun"  : {
"sample"  :   true  ,
"estimatedCredits"  :   0.01  ,
"creditsFormula"  :   "0.01 credits per call"  ,
"note"  :   "Sample data generated from the output schema. Nothing ran and no credits were used."
}
}


```


The` runContext.action` above is shortened; the real one carries every field the action’s output schema declares. Read it for its shape, not its values: they are generated from the schema, and no provider was called. What the dry run does check for real:


- **Your inputs.**` --data` that does not match the action’s input schema fails with the missing or wrong fields, for example` {"errors":\["Missing required field: linkedinUrl"\]}` , which is the same mistake a real run would reject.
- **The price.**` estimatedCredits` is the price of one call for these inputs. For a metered action, it is the price of one unit or one block of units, and` creditsFormula` says what it scales with.


Two limits. A dry run covers connector and native actions only: a tool or an agent runs a workspace’s own workflow, so only a real run shows its output. And an action whose output depends on its configuration (which object type, which sheet) has no fixed shape to sample, so the dry run says so instead of inventing one.


## 4. Plan a project offline#


A Cargo project declares a workspace in TypeScript (models, plays, agents, connectors) and is deployed with a plan and apply, like infrastructure code. You can write one and plan it before the workspace exists:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   project   init   acme-gtm
cd   acme-gtm
npm   install                # the project's own dependencies
cargo-ai   project   types     # typed integration actions and connector configs
cargo-ai   project   check     # validate every resource, no API calls
cargo-ai   project   plan      # the diff


```


Signed out, each step tells you what it skipped:


- **` types`** writes types for the official integrations: their actions, connector and extractor configs, and agent triggers. Model columns, language models and your connectors are read from a workspace, so those types arrive when you sign in and re-run` cargo-ai project types` .
- **` plan`** diffs against the state the project last deployed. With no state yet, every resource plans as a create. A project already bound to a workspace plans against the last cached read of its state, and says it may be stale. The per-record DNS diff of a domain is skipped, because it is read from the live zone.
- **` check`** and **` info`** never call the API, signed in or not.


` cargo-ai project deploy` is the step that needs an account.


## 5. Browse the catalog from any agent over MCP#


For an agent without a shell, or one you do not want installing a CLI, Cargo serves the action catalog as an MCP server that needs no token:


text


```text
https://mcp.getcargo.io/public


```


**Claude Code:**


shellscript


```text
claude   mcp   add   --transport   http   cargo-public   https://mcp.getcargo.io/public


```


**Cursor** , in` ~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or` .cursor/mcp.json` (one project):


json


```text
{
"mcpServers"  : {
"cargo-public"  : {
"url"  :   "https://mcp.getcargo.io/public"
}
}
}


```


There is no sign-in prompt. The server has two tools, with the same names and schemas as on the authenticated server:


- **` search_actions`** finds connector and native actions, each with its price in` credits\[\].cost` , exactly like` action list` above.
- **` get_action_schema`** returns an action’s input schema, and its output schema when the action declares a fixed one.


It runs nothing and spends nothing. Workspace tools and agents are not in it, an` Authorization` header sent to it is ignored, and requests are rate-limited per address. Because both servers share tool names, an agent that learned the catalog here calls` https://mcp.getcargo.io/mcp` the same way once you sign in.


## Sign up when you are ready#


Sign-up is the sign-in command. It runs in the terminal, with no browser and no card:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com                   # sends a code
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com   --code   123456     # creates the account on first use
cargo-ai   whoami


```


A new account starts with 100 free credits and no card, per the CLI’s sign-up notice. Then everything above carries over:


- **Run the action you dry ran.** The same command without` --dry-run` runs it and bills the credits; add` --wait-until-finished` to get back the finished run whose shape the dry run showed you.
- **Deploy the project.** Re-run` cargo-ai project types` for the workspace types, then` cargo-ai project plan` for a live diff and` cargo-ai project deploy` .
- **Switch the MCP server.** Point your client at` https://mcp.getcargo.io/mcp` , which signs you in with OAuth and adds` execute_action` , batches and your data models.


The full setup for a coding agent, skills included, is in[run go-to-market from Claude Code](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/run-go-to-market-from-claude-code) and[run go-to-market from Codex, Cursor or OpenCode](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/run-go-to-market-from-codex-cursor-opencode) .


## Frequently asked questions#


### Can I try Cargo without an account?


Yes, for everything that does not run or deploy. Without an account,` cargo-ai orchestration action list` shows every connector and native action with its credit price,` cargo-ai orchestration action execute --dry-run` returns a free sample result and the price of one call, and` cargo-ai project plan` plans a project offline. The MCP server at` https://mcp.getcargo.io/public` serves the same catalog with no token.


### Is there a demo API key or a sandbox workspace?


No. Signed-out commands read the public catalog, and nothing signed out can run an action or hold data. To run anything, create an account with` cargo-ai login --email you@company.com` .


### Does a dry run cost credits?


No. A dry run calls no provider and creates no run: it validates your inputs against the action’s schema, prices the call, and generates a sample from the output schema.` creditsUsedCount` is 0 and the result is marked` "dryRun"` .


### How do I see what a Cargo action costs before signing up?


Run` cargo-ai orchestration action list <keywords>` and read the` credits` array on each result, or call` search_actions` on` https://mcp.getcargo.io/public` . For the price of one call with your inputs, run the action with` --dry-run` and read` dryRun.estimatedCredits` .


### Can I deploy a Cargo project without an account?


No.` init` ,` types` ,` check` ,` info` and` plan` work signed out, so you can write and validate a project first.` cargo-ai project deploy` needs a signed-in workspace to deploy to.
